content: Individuals diagnosed with diabetes who experience vision loss should be promptly referred to a vision rehabilitation specialist. This referral is essential to help optimize their remaining visual function and improve their overall quality of life. These individuals should also receive comprehensive education on managing vision loss. This includes providing them with resources for self-care and ensuring they are aware of the risks associated with hypoglycemia, which may be more challenging to detect due to impaired vision. Vision loss in diabetic patients can lead to significant difficulties in daily functioning, an increased risk of social isolation, and challenges to emotional well-being. Vision rehabilitation programs are designed to address these issues by promoting independence, enhancing quality of life, and fostering better social engagement. These programs focus on managing both the psychological and physical impacts of vision impairment, ensuring a holistic approach to care.
